raw_case_text:
A 50-year-old Chinese male presented to a local hospital with right ankle pain and limited mobility 23 months ago and underwent a synovectomy of the ankle. Specimen culture revealed brucellosis infection in sheep. The patient came to the department of Orthopaedics of our hospital 18 months ago because his symptoms did not improve. His case history indicated that he had worked in a Sheep farm for 9 months. We, therefore, suspected that he might have acquired Brucella infection through ingestion or contact with injured skin. A 37 C temperature, no sweating, weight loss, and no personal or family history of tuberculosis were all present on admission. Physical examination showed significant tenderness on the lateral side of the right ankle without fever. Blood flow to right toe is good, right ankle varus pressure test is positive. Laboratory tests were as follows: Hemoglobin (Hb) 136 g/L, Red blood cell count (RBC) 4.25x1012/L, White blood cell (WBC) 10.09x109/L accompanied by neutrophil elevation, Platelet 363x109/ L, Erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) 31 mm/h, C-reactive protein (CRP) 32 mg/L. Rose-Bengal Plate Agglutination Test (RBPT) was positive.
Anteroposterior and lateral X-ray of the right ankle showed arrowed joint spaces (Figure 1A and B). CT showed multiple cysts were noted below the articular surface of the right ankle, and the articular surface of the talus collapsed (Figure 2A-D). MRI showed the right ankle joint space was significantly narrowed, the articular surface was coarse, the articular cartilage was thinned, the talus articular surface collapsed, and multiple cysts were found in the subchondral bone (Figure 3A-D). Joint synovial fluid of right ankle was extracted by joint aspiration and sent to the laboratory for Real-time PCR examination, and the results showed that there was B. melitensis in the synovial fluid (Figure 4). The HE staining of ankle fluid revealed inflammatory cell infiltration, while acid-fast staining was negative (Figure 5A and B). We concluded that the patient had recurrent Brucella ankle arthritis and was treated with doxycycline (0.1 g po bid), rifampicin (0.6 g po qd) and cefotaxime-sulbactam (2.25 g ivgtt q8h) for six weeks during hospitalization. ESR and CRP levels declined significantly after drug treatment, returning to normal levels of 17.00 mm/h and 7.88 mg/L, respectively.     
The right ankle movement of the patient was basically normal at discharge, and the pain was significantly reduced. Laboratory tests after drug treatment showed erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) and C-reactive protein (CRP) levels of 17.00 mm/h and 7.88 mg/L, respectively, significantly decreased and returned to normal. At following-up 18 months later, the patient had no discomfort in the right ankle and all inflammatory markers were normal. RBPT was negative.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 50-year-old male presented with persistent right ankle pain and restricted mobility for eighteen months following prior ankle surgery.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The patient initially developed right ankle pain and stiffness 23 months prior and underwent an ankle synovectomy at an outside hospital. Due to lack of clinical improvement over the subsequent 18 months, he was referred for orthopedic evaluation of persistent pain and joint dysfunction, without constitutional fevers or night sweats.
subjective.past_medical_history: History of right ankle synovectomy 23 months prior for septic arthritis. Denied personal or family history of tuberculosis. Epidemiological exposure/Occupation: Worked on a sheep farm for 9 months with potential percutaneous or mucosal exposure.
subjective.review_of_systems: Denies fever, night sweats, or unintentional weight loss. Home medications: None documented. Allergies: None documented.

objective.physical_examination: Right ankle: Significant localized tenderness over the lateral aspect of the right ankle, restricted range of motion, and positive ankle varus stress test. Peripheral perfusion: Intact distal pulses and capillary refill in the right toes. Afebrile (temperature 37.0 °C).
objective.routine_investigations: Admission labs: Hemoglobin 136 g/L, RBC 4.25 x 10^12/L, WBC 10.09 x 10^9/L with neutrophil predominance, platelets 363 x 10^9/L, ESR 31 mm/h, CRP 32 mg/L. Post-treatment labs (6 weeks): ESR normalized to 17.00 mm/h and CRP normalized to 7.88 mg/L. Follow-up labs (18 months): Normal inflammatory markers.
objective.advanced_workup: Right ankle X-ray: Marked narrowing of the tibiotalar joint space. Right ankle CT: Multiple subchondral cyst formations below the articular surface with collapse of the talar dome. Right ankle MRI: Severe joint space narrowing, irregular and eroded articular surfaces, severe cartilage thinning, subchondral cysts, and talar collapse. Synovial fluid analysis: H&E staining demonstrated acute-on-chronic inflammatory cell infiltration; acid-fast bacilli staining was negative.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation:
Definitive diagnosis: Recurrent chronic brucellar septic arthritis of the right ankle with secondary talar osteonecrosis and subchondral collapse, confirmed by real-time PCR detection of Brucella melitensis in right ankle synovial aspirate, positive Rose Bengal Plate Test (RBPT), and prior synovial culture from first surgery growing Brucella from sheep contact. Tuberculosis excluded by negative acid-fast stain.
Plan & Clinical Course: Received 6 weeks of inpatient combination antimicrobial therapy comprising oral doxycycline 0.1 g twice daily, oral rifampicin 0.6 g once daily, and IV cefotaxime-sulbactam 2.25 g every 8 hours. The patient experienced marked pain relief, restoration of normal ankle motion, normalization of ESR and CRP, and at 18-month follow-up remained completely asymptomatic with negative RBPT serology.
